prompt: A reservoir holds $1000$ cubic meters of water at $t = 0$. Water flows in at a constant $20$ m³ per hour and is pumped out at a rate of $2t$ m³ per hour, for $0 \le t \le 8$ hours. How much water is in the reservoir at $t = 8$, in cubic meters?
hint: Net rate $=$ in $-$ out $= 20 - 2t$. The change in water is the integral of the net rate.

hints.text: Net rate $=$ in $-$ out $= 20 - 2t$. The change in water is the integral of the net rate.
Change $= 96$ m³, so the reservoir holds $1000 + 96 = 1096$ m³.

explanation: Final amount: $1000 + 96 = 1096$ m³. (The outflow $2t$ overtakes the inflow $20$ only at $t = 10$, so the level is still rising at $t = 8$, just more slowly.)

alternativeExplanations.title: In and out separately
steps: Total out: $\int_0^8 2t \, dt = 64$ m³ (a triangle of base $8$ and height $16$).
